$comment: House colours by era and district (house kit K3, world QA defect W-37). The pipeline and the renderer pick a house's wall (body), trim, and for the Marina a roof-edge tile colour from here wherever they draw a house today (the pastel class of pipeline/lib/mesh.ts facadeStyle: residential, or under 16 m and not an office; the glass, industrial, masonry and concrete classes keep their own colours). src/content/housePalettes.ts assignHouseColours does the picking: the first rule that matches the house's assessor year and its DataSF Analysis Neighborhood picks the palette, a hash of the building id picks the body, and a body already worn by a touching neighbour (footprints within maxGapM) is skipped, so no two adjacent houses on a block face share a colour. Overrides are hand palettes for named rows and win over the rules. Colours are sRGB hex; saturation means HSV saturation, (max - min) / max, as the houses audit measured it.

rules.note: Italianate, Stick, Queen Anne and Edwardian rows: saturated bodies with contrasting trim, plus white and grey bodies with coloured trim.
The Marina's 1920s and 1930s Mediterranean stucco: cream and ochre, red tile at the roof edge.
The Sunset, the Richmond and the southern row-house tracts of the 1920s to 1950s: pastels and white.
Interwar and postwar stucco elsewhere: sand, dove grey, pale terracotta, sage.
1990 and later: greys, with more glazing.
No assessor year: the city's middle register.

overrides.label: Postcard Row, the east side of the 700 block of Steiner St
overrides.note: The seven Painted Ladies facing Alamo Square (710 to 722 Steiner St, built 1892 to 1896; the assessor roll says 1898 and 1900). Confirmed from the committed sf world: the seven consecutive lots 0803017 to 0803023 of assessor block 0803 front the Steiner centreline (8.0 to 10.6 m from it) between the Hayes St node (south) and the Grove St node (north), 13.1 to 15.7 m tall. The other two candidates the houses audit listed stand back from the street: 201006.0088534 (lot 024, 31.5 m back, a rear cottage) and 201006.0072707 (lot 013, 22.3 m back, around the Hayes corner). Records are listed north (Grove) to south (Hayes). Hand colours, invented in the Victorian manner: no two neighbours share a body, and every trim contrasts with its body.
